absent: AUSENTE: Full list and removal data paths including path resolution helpers and mount write accounting and audit reporting and stale-detection internals.
AUSENTE: Extended-attribute handler registration and visibility rules plus packing of names into user buffers and size-probe behavior.
AUSENTE: Small-attribute cache allocation and limit accounting plus hash-table lifecycle and concurrent access rules.
AUSENTE: Executable loading sequence and interpreter selection and credential transformation and core-dump handling.
AUSENTE: Block buffer input-output submission and completion and migration and cache-lookup internals.
AUSENTE: Configuration filesystem object lifecycle and operation callbacks and attribute access semantics.
AUSENTE: Complete error-code matrix and permission checks and lock ordering across these interfaces.

findings.text: The list syscalls named llistxattr and flistxattr delegate to a shared at-style helper, the former supplying cwd context with no-follow behavior and the latter supplying an open descriptor with empty-path semantics.

Removal syscalls named removexattrat and removexattr plus lremovexattr and fremovexattr all funnel into one at-style remover, differing only in directory descriptor and pathname inputs and in follow versus no-follow versus empty-path selection.
The at-style remover accepts only no-follow and empty-path option bits and rejects any other bit pattern reporting EINVAL before importing names or resolving paths.

Removal by name first tests for POSIX access-control naming and diverts matching requests to access-control deletion, while all other names use the generic removal path under the caller's mount identity mapping.

When the pathname argument is absent the remover operates on the descriptor-backed file after auditing it under a write hold, otherwise it resolves the pathname with symlink traversal governed by the no-follow selection.
Pathname-based removal retries resolution with revalidation forced when the first attempt reports staleness, giving lookup a second chance before the error is returned.

The generic list helper walks the filesystem attribute handler table, skipping entries lacking a name prefix or declined by their visibility predicate, and accumulates surviving prefixes into the caller buffer while tracking remaining space, returning consumed length or the first packing fault.

Allocation for a small attribute value fails fast on a missing value pointer and on size arithmetic wrap, otherwise reserves accounted memory and records the payload length alongside a copy of the supplied bytes.

Release of a small attribute tolerates a null handle, otherwise frees the name string and then the container via the virtual-aware releaser, with a read-copy-update callback adapting the same path for deferred reclamation.

Small-attribute identity combines the owning list head address with the full name string under a seeded hash, with distinct entry and object hash entry points plus an equality test comparing both parent linkage and lexical name, and table parameters enabling automatic shrinking.

Insertion binds the new entry to its parent list, places it in the lazily allocated hash, then appends it to the list with read-copy-update ordering; the bounded variant pre-charges size limits and refunds the charge if insertion fails.

The execution parameter block aggregates address-space anchors and replacement tracking, execution identity and namespace, a set of single-bit control markers for descriptor passing and privilege and commitment state, file references for executable and interpreter and loader, credential staging, argument counts, filename and interpreter name views, preserved stack limits, and a fixed-size header scratch area.
The misc-format helper record holds a read-only interpreter roster reference plus the handler-chosen interpreter name and file and argument string together with a wide flag word.

A binary format handler links into a global roster, pins its owner module, and offers an executable-loading callback with an optional core-dump callback paired with a minimum dump threshold when dumps are configured.
The misc-format registry combines a hashed entry table with a dedicated spin guard and a boolean enable switch, laid out with randomization for hardening.
The core-name size ceiling named CORENAME_MAX_SIZE is 128.
Selectors named EXSTACK_DEFAULT and EXSTACK_DISABLE_X and EXSTACK_ENABLE_X carry values 0 and 1 and 2 in order.

Execution flag positions place enforce-no-dump at bit zero and path-inaccessible at bit two with preserve-argv-zero at bit three and transparent-interpreter at bit four, each mask being one shifted by its position, yielding masks one and four and eight and sixteen in the same order.

The block buffer descriptor aggregates a state bitmask and a ring link for peers on the same page, a union covering page versus folio views, block number with size and intra-page data address, backing device, completion-private opaque pointer, association and metadata linkage, an atomic user count, and a dedicated completion guard.

Buffer lifecycle moves through validity and dirtiness, exclusive access and submission tracking, on-disk placement including fresh and delayed and not-yet-written variants, asynchronous read and write activity, contiguity boundaries, write-failure marking, quiet error handling, metadata and priority hints, deferred completion, migration, and a private-use floor that is not itself a state.
The per-page buffer ceiling divides the platform page size by five hundred twelve.

Per-state helpers provide idempotent set and clear plus a readback test for each lifecycle bit, with test-and-set and test-and-clear forms for contended transitions, and the validity setter skips work when already set while pairing an ordering barrier with the matching acquire-side read.
The page-to-header accessor requires the private marker and yields the first header, while indexed selection walks the peer ring the requested distance and takes an additional reference on arrival.

Superblock block helpers cover synchronous read with movable versus unmovable reclaim hints, fire-and-forget prefetch, allocation-or-fetch with filesystem-reclaim exclusion and no-fail behavior, and cache-only lookup in both blocking and nonblocking flavors.
Mapping a header records the placed state together with the owning device and starting block number and the filesystem block size.
Batch submission distinguishes a synchronous multi-buffer read from a prefetch variant that carries caller-supplied operation flags and skips waiting.

Forgetting a header tolerates null input, while fallback helpers make initialization and invalidation no-ops, freeing always succeeds, sync reports success, presence checks report absent, and the over-limit indicator stays clear.

Registry and completion safety relies on a spin guard for misc-format entries, a per-page completion guard serializing sibling input-output finish, plus read-copy-update list ordering and hashed-table insertion discipline for small attributes.

A configuration node stores a name pointer with a small inline name buffer, a reference count, sibling linkage, parent and group back-pointers, a type descriptor link, and a dentry for its filesystem representation.
A node-type record pins its owner module and references item-level and group-level operation tables alongside text-attribute and binary-attribute arrays.
A configuration group embeds a full node as its header and adds a child roster, a subsystem link, a default-subgroup roster, and a queue node for membership in its parent defaults.
Text attributes expose name plus owner plus mode with show and store callbacks, while binary siblings extend that header with a private opaque pointer and a maximum size plus read and write handlers.

Small helpers return the stored name pointer, safely cast a node to its enclosing group with null tolerance, propagate reference acquisition and release through the embedded node, and queue a new default subgroup at the tail of its parent list.
The inline configuration-name buffer length named CONFIGFS_ITEM_NAME_LEN is 20.

List and removal paths surface helper errors directly, reject unknown option bits, report missing descriptors, and retry only staleness, so callers must treat flag and descriptor faults separately from transient lookup staleness.
Buffer headers require reference discipline across peer walks and ordered completion guarding for sibling input-output, while quiet marking requests silenced error reporting.
Each public header defines a unique inclusion guard macro so repeated inclusion is harmless.
Buffer folio-migration hooks are defined as null placeholders.
